ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
protocol_type: Strict 46-bit transaction protocol over 2-wire half-duplex serial: 8-bit Request (host) + 1-bit Turnaround + 3-bit ACK (target) + 32-bit Data + 1-bit Data Parity + 1-bit Turnaround. The Request packet's APnDP + RnW + A[2:3] bits select which DP or AP register is being read or written. AP register banking goes through the DP SELECT register first.

request_packet_format.transmit_order: LSB first on SWDIO synchronous to SWCLK rising edges

field_breakdown.name: Start
field_breakdown.description: Always 1 — marks the beginning of a request packet.

field_breakdown.name: APnDP
field_breakdown.description: Selects which register space: DP (debug port) or AP (access port).

field_breakdown.name: A[2]
field_breakdown.description: Register address bit 2 — together with A[3] selects one of four registers per bank.

field_breakdown.name: Parity
field_breakdown.description: Even parity over APnDP + RnW + A[2] + A[3] — the target checks; mismatch causes the target to ignore the transaction (or sets WDATAERR on writes).

field_breakdown.name: Stop
field_breakdown.description: Always 0 — marks the end of the request packet.

field_breakdown.name: Park
field_breakdown.description: Always 1 — drives SWDIO HIGH before the host releases SWDIO for the upcoming Turnaround.

ack_packet_format.transmit_order: LSB first on SWDIO synchronous to SWCLK rising edges (target-driven)

valid_codes.name: OK
valid_codes.meaning: Target accepted the request; for reads, target now drives 33-bit data field; for writes, host now drives 33-bit data field.

valid_codes.name: WAIT
valid_codes.meaning: Target is busy (e.g. previous AP transaction still in flight). Host must retry the same request. Data field is meaningless and shall be ignored (or driven as zeros for protocol robustness).

valid_codes.name: FAULT
valid_codes.meaning: A sticky error has occurred (read CTRL/STAT to identify; write ABORT to clear, then retry). Data field is meaningless.

ack_packet_format.invalid_codes: Any 3-bit pattern other than 001/010/100 is a protocol error. Host should perform a 50-cycle line reset followed by an IDCODE/DPIDR read.

data_packet_format.transmit_order: LSB first on SWDIO synchronous to SWCLK rising edges
data_packet_format.parity_rule: Single-bit even parity over the 32 data bits (the 33rd bit shall make the XOR of all 33 bits = 0). On writes, host generates parity; target checks. On reads, target generates parity; host checks.
data_packet_format.direction: Host-driven on writes, target-driven on reads.

phase_2_turnaround_a.description: 1-bit Turnaround period — SWDIO transitions from host-driven (after Park=1) to target-driven (ready to drive ACK).

phase_4_data.direction: write: host → target / read: target → host

phase_5_parity.description: 1-bit Data Parity (even parity over the 32 data bits).

phase_6_turnaround_b.description: 1-bit Turnaround period — SWDIO transitions back to host-driven (host ready for next request).

dp_register_catalog.name: ABORT
dp_register_catalog.purpose: Write-1-to-clear sticky errors; write DAPABORT=1 to abort an in-flight AP transaction.

dp_register_catalog.name: IDCODE/DPIDR
dp_register_catalog.purpose: Identifies the DP: DESIGNER (JEP106 manufacturer ID), PARTNO (DP part number), VERSION, REVISION, MIN (min DP version).

dp_register_catalog.name: CTRL/STAT
dp_register_catalog.access: Read/Write (depends on DPBANKSEL — bank 0 is CTRL/STAT, bank 1..4 are DLCR/TARGETID/DLPIDR/EVENTSTAT)

dp_register_catalog.name: SELECT
dp_register_catalog.purpose: Bank select for AP and DP: APSEL[31:24]=AP index, APBANKSEL[7:4]=AP bank (high 4 bits of AP register offset), DPBANKSEL[3:0]=DP bank.

dp_register_catalog.name: RDBUFF
dp_register_catalog.purpose: Returns the data of the previous posted AP read; reading RDBUFF flushes the posted-read queue and is the standard way to recover the final read result of a burst.

dp_register_catalog.name: TARGETID
dp_register_catalog.purpose: ADIv5.1+; identifies the target SoC: TPARTNO + TDESIGNER + TREVISION.

dp_register_catalog.name: DLPIDR
dp_register_catalog.purpose: ADIv5.1+; multi-drop SWD target instance: PROTVSN + TINSTANCE; used with TARGETSEL for multi-drop addressing.

dp_register_catalog.name: EVENTSTAT
dp_register_catalog.purpose: ADIv5.1+; per-target event status (e.g. CPU halted on target).

ap_address_decoding.ap_address_bits_per_register: A[3:2] (selected by Request bits A[2], A[3])
ap_address_decoding.ap_bank_selection: SELECT.APBANKSEL[7:4] selects the high 4 bits of the AP register offset (each bank is 16 bytes = 4 × 32-bit registers)
ap_address_decoding.ap_index_selection: SELECT.APSEL[31:24] (8 bits) selects which of up to 256 APs is being accessed

memap_register_catalog.name: CSW
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Control & Status Word — AddrInc[5:4] (Off/Single/Packed), Size[2:0] (8/16/32/64-bit), DbgSwEnable, Prot[6:0], Mode[3:0], TrInProg (busy), DeviceEn.

memap_register_catalog.name: TAR
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Transfer Address Register — the 32-bit system-bus address used by the next DRW transfer; auto-incremented per CSW.AddrInc; ADIv5.2 supports a 64-bit TARLO+TARHI pair.

memap_register_catalog.name: DRW
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Data Read/Write — the data field; read returns the value at TAR (and triggers a system-bus read with auto-increment of TAR); write pushes the value to TAR on the system bus.

memap_register_catalog.name: BD0
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Banked Data 0 — directly addressed system-bus access at TAR[31:4]+0x00 without modifying TAR (allows 4-word bursts without TAR-overflow concerns).

memap_register_catalog.name: MBT
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Memory Barrier Transfer — issues a barrier on the system bus to flush write buffers (optional, signaled by IDR.Type).

memap_register_catalog.name: CFG
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Configuration — Big-endian flag, Long-address (64-bit TAR), Large-data (>32-bit DRW) support indicators.

memap_register_catalog.name: BASE
memap_register_catalog.purpose: ROM Table base address — bits[31:12] point to the 4 KB CoreSight ROM Table that enumerates this AP's debug components.

memap_register_catalog.name: IDR
memap_register_catalog.purpose: Identification Register — Type (AP type code: 0=JTAG-AP, 1=AMBA AHB-AP, 2=APB-AP, 4=AXI-AP, etc.), Variant, Class, JEP106 designer.

channels.name: SWCLK
channels.description: Serial Wire Clock. Host-driven free-running clock during a transaction; idle level not specified. Target samples SWDIO on the rising edge during host-driven phases; target drives SWDIO before the next rising edge during target-driven phases.

channels.name: SWDIO
channels.description: Serial Wire Data Input/Output. Host-driven during Request and Data-Write phases; target-driven during ACK and Data-Read phases; 1-bit Turnaround periods cover the direction-change cycles.

valid_ready_handshake_rules: Explicit Turnaround: a 1-bit Turnaround SWCLK cycle is mandatory between every host-driven phase and target-driven phase. CTRL/STAT.TRNCNT may extend this to up to 2-4 cycles for slow-driver or shared-pin scenarios.
Per-transaction ACK: target signals OK/WAIT/FAULT in every transaction; OK proceeds normally, WAIT signals 'busy, retry', FAULT signals sticky-error.

Posted reads: for AP reads, the OK ACK confirms the previous transaction's data was captured; the read-N data is delivered at the OK ACK of transaction N+1 (or via DP.RDBUFF if N is the last read in a burst).
No per-byte CRC — single-bit parity over Request fields and over the 32-bit Data field is the only protocol-layer integrity check.
Line reset: 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO=HIGH unconditionally returns the SW-DP to a known state; followed by an IDCODE/DPIDR read.

frame_format.byte_breakdown: 8-bit Request + 1-bit Turnaround + 3-bit ACK + 32-bit Data + 1-bit Parity + 1-bit Turnaround = 46 bits.
frame_format.bit_order: LSB first throughout — Request bits 0..7 in order, ACK bits 0..2 in order, Data bits 0..31 in order, Parity at bit 32.
frame_format.line_reset_sequence: At least 50 SWCLK cycles with SWDIO held HIGH; resets the SW-DP wire-level state and selects DP register space for the next Request.
